# verda template

Manage reusable resource templates

Save, list, show, and delete reusable resource configuration templates.
Templates pre-fill the create wizard so you don't repeat the same settings.

Aliases: `tmpl`

Subcommands:

- [`verda template create`](#verda-template-create): Create a new resource template interactively
- [`verda template delete`](#verda-template-delete): Delete a saved template
- [`verda template edit`](#verda-template-edit): Edit fields of an existing template
- [`verda template list`](#verda-template-list): List saved templates
- [`verda template show`](#verda-template-show): Show details of a saved template

## verda template create

Create a new resource template interactively

Create a reusable resource configuration template by running
the interactive wizard. The wizard collects instance type,
image, location, SSH keys, storage, and other settings.

Templates are saved as YAML files under ~/.verda/templates/&lt;resource&gt;/.
Names are auto-reformatted: "My GPU Setup" becomes "my-gpu-setup".

After saving, use "verda vm create --from &lt;name&gt;" to create
instances with pre-filled settings.

You can manually edit the template YAML to add features like:

```text
hostname_pattern: "gpu-{random}-{location}"
storage_skip: true
startup_script_skip: true
```

**Usage**

```text
verda template create [name] [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Create a template interactively
verda template create

# Create with a name (skips name prompt)
verda template create gpu-training

# Then use it to create VMs
verda vm create --from gpu-training
verda vm create --from gpu-training --hostname my-vm
```

## verda template delete

Delete a saved template

Delete a saved resource configuration template.
Without arguments, shows an interactive picker with confirmation.
The argument must be in resource/name format (e.g. vm/gpu-training).
Agent mode requires the template argument and --yes.

**Usage**

```text
verda template delete [resource/name] [flags]
```

Aliases: `rm`

**Flags**

```text
      --yes   Skip confirmation for destructive actions (required in agent mode)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Interactive picker
verda template delete

# Delete a VM template
verda template delete vm/gpu-training

# Short alias
verda tmpl rm vm/gpu-training

# Agent mode
verda --agent template delete vm/gpu-training --yes
```

## verda template edit

Edit fields of an existing template

Edit specific fields of an existing template. Shows a menu of
all template fields with their current values — pick which ones
to change.

Without arguments, shows an interactive template picker first.

**Usage**

```text
verda template edit [resource/name] [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Interactive picker, then field menu
verda template edit

# Edit a specific template
verda template edit vm/gpu-training
```

## verda template list

List saved templates

List all saved resource configuration templates.
Use --type to filter by resource type (e.g. "vm").

**Usage**

```text
verda template list [flags]
```

Aliases: `ls`

**Flags**

```text
      --type string   Filter by resource type (e.g. vm)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# List all templates
verda template list

# List only VM templates
verda template list --type vm

# Short alias
verda tmpl ls
```

## verda template show

Show details of a saved template

Display the full configuration of a saved template.
Without arguments, shows an interactive picker.
The argument must be in resource/name format (e.g. vm/gpu-training).

**Usage**

```text
verda template show [resource/name] [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Interactive picker
verda template show

# Show a VM template
verda template show vm/gpu-training

# Output as JSON
verda template show vm/gpu-training -o json
```

---

Global flags such as `--output`, `--agent` and `--debug` work with every command: see [Global Flags](../commands.md#global-flags).
